summary: Edwards Lifesciences has asked customers to remove from inventory some delivery systems used for Sapien M3 transcatheter mitral valve replacement after receiving three reports of balloons bursting during inflation, the Food and Drug Administration said Thursday in an early alert. Edwards reported one death and one serious injury associated with the problem as of Oct. 5, when the device maker sent a letter to customers recommending they remove the Commander M systems from where they are used or sold and return them to the company. The issue could lead to an embolism or prevent the physician from retrieving the device through the guide sheath, requiring an additional intervention such as surgery, the FDA said. The potentially high-risk intervention carries a risk of serious adverse health consequences.
title: Edwards recall of Sapien mitral delivery systems tied to 1 death

summary: Medtronic exchanged all of its remaining shares of the diabetes technology spinoff.
title: MiniMed completes separation from Medtronic

summary: The American Medical Association has released a new governance framework to ensure the safe and effective use of AI agents in healthcare. The framework is based on the principle that for agentic AI solutions to perform clinical functions, they must be backed by evidence and maintain high-quality performance. It provides four questions focused on which tasks AI tools should be allowed to perform and in which situations, as well as who is accountable for the tools' actions.
title: AMA releases governance framework for agentic AI in healthcare

title: EndoQuest Robotics hires chief commercial officer

summary: Results of a Dexcom-funded study published in the New England Journal of Medicine Wednesday demonstrated that people with Type 2 diabetes who don’t take insulin may benefit from wearing a continuous glucose monitor. Dexcom first shared the results at the American Diabetes Association’s Scientific Sessions this summer. The study found that people who wore a CGM had a larger reduction in hemoglobin A1c than people who received routine care after 26 weeks. The published results come as diabetes tech firms anticipate the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to expand Medicare coverage of CGMs for people with diabetes who don’t take insulin. Having a peer-reviewed publication in a leading medical journal “should be a catalyst” for a CMS decision, William Blair analysts wrote in a research note.
title: NEJM study supports CGM use for people with diabetes who don’t take insulin

summary: Labcorp has agreed to buy certain laboratory testing businesses from Opko Health subsidiary BioReference Health for $722 million, plus an additional sum of up to $150 million tied to revenue from a prostate cancer blood test. The final purchase price could be adjusted based on closing revenues, the companies said Thursday. Labcorp is acquiring businesses focused on clinical and women's health testing services, urology and diagnostic services provided to correctional institutions. The deal also adds more than 80 patient service centers to Labcorp’s network. In addition, the lab services provider is gaining BioReference Health's 4Kscore test, which has Food and Drug Administration approval to help predict the likelihood of finding aggressive prostate cancer before a biopsy decision.
title: Labcorp to buy BioReference assets for up to $872M

summary: Zimmer Biomet said Tuesday it has inked a multi-year extension to its exclusive distribution agreement with Think Surgical. The deal, which extends an agreement signed in 2024, positions Zimmer to continue distributing an exclusive version of Think’s TMINI wireless handheld miniature robotic system. Zimmer’s exclusive version of TMINI is compatible with its Persona knee system, a personalized product used in total knee replacements.
title: Zimmer and Think Surgical pen multi-year extension to robotic surgery deal

summary: Siemens Healthineers said Monday that it will no longer sell general imaging ultrasound systems, focusing instead on ultrasound used in procedural imaging. The company will focus on systems used in interventional cardiology and electrophysiology procedures. Siemens Healthineers said this approach will allow it to bring together its imaging systems, software capabilities and partnerships with heart device companies to support physicians in increasingly complex procedures. Siemens Healthineers said it will continue to provide support for its general ultrasound systems, including maintenance, software updates and transducer availability.
title: Siemens Healthineers to stop selling general ultrasound systems

title: Orthofix pays former executives $24M in damages

summary: Agilent said Tuesday that it has agreed to buy digital pathology software provider Proscia for $240 million upfront. The deal, which includes up to $30 million in milestones, will give Agilent control of technology that connects slide scanners, laboratory information systems and other parts of the pathology workflow. Agilent’s deal comes months after Roche agreed to buy PathAI for up to $1.05 billion. Evercore ISI analysts noted that Agilent “got the rights to play in this market at a lower price point.”
title: Agilent to buy Proscia for $240M
